# Policy enforcement overview

This topic provides overview information about policies in HCP Terraform. Policies are rules that let you validate that Terraform plans comply with security rules and best practices. You can use Terraform policy with both workspaces and Stacks. Sentinel and OPA policy sets only support workspaces.

## Introduction

You can implement policies using one of the following frameworks:
- Terraform policy (beta): Native HCL-based policy framework
- Sentinel: HashiCorp's legacy policy-as-code framework
- OPA: Open Policy Agent with Rego language

You can implement policies that check for any number of conditions, such as whether infrastructure configuration adheres to security standards or best practices. For example, you may want to write a policy to check whether Terraform plans to deploy production infrastructure to the correct region.

You can also use policies to enforce standards for your organization’s workflows. For example, you could write a policy to prevent new infrastructure deployments on Fridays, reducing the risk of production incidents outside of your team’s working hours.

## Workflow

You can apply Terraform policy sets with both workspaces and Stacks, while Sentinel and OPA are only supported for workspaces.

- **Workspaces**: Policies evaluate during workspace runs. Refer to [Policy enforcement for workspaces](/terraform/cloud-docs/workspaces/policy-enforcement) to learn how to manage and evaluate policies for workspaces.
- **Stacks**: Policies evaluate during each deployment run within a Stack. Refer to [Policy enforcement for Stacks](/terraform/cloud-docs/stacks/policy-enforcement) to learn how to manage and evaluate policies for Stacks.

The following workflow describes how to create and manage policies.

### Author policies

You can author policies in the appropriate format for the policy framework of your choice, or implement pre-written Terraform policy or Sentinel policies maintained by HashiCorp. Pre-written policies enforce common standards, such as PCI DSS. Refer to [Use HashiCorp managed pre-written policies](/terraform/cloud-docs/policy-enforcement/prewritten) to learn how to use pre-written policies.

To learn how to author your own policies, refer to the appropriate documentation for the policy framework of your choice:

- [Define policies for the Terraform policy framework](/terraform/cloud/policy-enforcement/define-policies/terraform-policy)
- [Define Sentinel policies in HCP Terraform](/terraform/cloud/policy-enforcement/define-policies/custom-sentinel)
- [Define Open Policy Agent policies for HCP Terraform](/terraform/cloud/policy-enforcement/define-policies/opa)

### Create policy sets

To enforce poicies in HCP Terraform, configure a policy set. Policy sets can use pre-written policies, or your own policies either managed individually, in a VCS repository, or with the HCP Terraform API.

- To use pre-written policies, refer to [Pre-written policy library](/terraform/cloud-docs/policy-enforcement/pre-written).
- To use Terraform policy, refer to [Configure a Terraform policy set with a VCS repository](/terraform/cloud-docs/policy-enforcement/manage-policy-sets/terraform-policy-vcs).
- To use Sentinel, refer to [Configure a Sentinel policy set with a VCS repository](/terraform/cloud-docs/policy-enforcement/manage-policy-sets/sentinel-vcs).
- To use OPA, refer to [Configure an OPA policy set with a VCS repository](/terraform/cloud-docs/policy-enforcement/manage-policy-sets/opa-vcs).

### Review policy results

HCP Terraform evaluates policies for each Terraform run on configured workspaces and Stacks. Depending on their [enforcement level](/terraform/cloud-docs/policy-enforcement/manage-policy-sets#policy-enforcement-levels), failed policies can stop the run. You can override failed policies with the right permissions.

For information about viewing policy results for workspaces, refer to [View policy results](/terraform/cloud-docs/workspaces/policy-enforcement/view-results) for workspaces. For information about policy evaluation in Stacks, refer to [View policy results](/terraform/cloud-docs/stacks/policy-enforcement) for Stacks.
